sources.title: Exact repository linked-list intersection question and verified mapping
Independent source-first linked-list intersection candidate review

claims.text: The source explicitly asks for the two-pointer idea to find an intersection node of two singly linked lists, but does not preserve cyclic-list semantics or a concrete node class.

Under the explicit finite acyclic identity-based intersection contract, switching each pointer to the other head after null returns the first shared node or null without mutating either list, in O(m+n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
The deterministic fixture covers ordinary/same-head/tail intersections, identity-vs-value, empty cases, and non-mutation.
Independent source-first review found no hard failures, unsupported claims or uncovered source variants and recompiled the exact candidate Java against exhaustive small-shape identity tests.

findings: The preserved source explicitly asks for the two-pointer idea for finding the intersection node of two singly linked lists; it does not preserve a node class, mutation policy, or cyclic-list semantics.

The candidate states its executable boundary instead of presenting it as recovered source: finite acyclic singly linked lists, reference-identity/shared-suffix intersection, first shared node or null, and no input mutation.

The switch-head mechanism is directly explained: A→B and B→A equalize the aggregate traversal length, so the prefix-length difference is canceled; the no-intersection path converges at null under the finite acyclic precondition.

The exact Java fence independently compiles on JDK 21 and an isolated property-style fixture exhaustively checks prefix lengths 0..5, shared suffix lengths 1..5, disjoint equal-valued lists, empty lists and non-mutation.

The answer explicitly rejects value equality as an intersection test, gives the length-alignment alternative, and routes cyclic lists to a separate boundary rather than claiming universal termination.
